title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: scope policies to users with adaptive scopes
notes: claim 61: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Pass: the roadmap details, entitlement, policy controls and PowerShell calls are supported. The scope-creation route could explain the remaining wizard choices, and Microsoft does not substantiate the assurance that monitored users see nothing different.

claims.claim: Communication Compliance policies can select adaptive scopes instead of All users or selected users and groups.
claims.quote: You can select All users, define specific users in a Communication Compliance policy, or select an adaptive scope.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Adaptive scope membership follows a query over directory attributes rather than a hand-maintained user list.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify, so you can define the membership of users or groups included in that query.

claims.claim: Supported user attributes include department, country or region, job title and Exchange custom attributes.
claims.quote: Job title Department Office Street address City State or province Postal code Country or region Email addresses Alias Exchange custom attributes: CustomAttribute1 - CustomAttribute15

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Adaptive membership queries run daily.
claims.quote: These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Adaptive scoping is admin-opt-in: existing user selection is not replaced unless an administrator creates and selects scopes.
claims.quote: To use an adaptive policy, create the adaptive scope before you create your policy, then select the scope when you choose this option.

claims.claim: The adaptive scope must exist before the Communication Compliance policy is created.
claims.quote: To use an adaptive policy, create the adaptive scope before you create your policy, then select the scope when you choose this option.

claims.claim: Users and Microsoft 365 Groups are the adaptive scope types applicable to Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: Select adaptive scopes: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify to define the membership of users or groups. ... Site scopes aren't applicable to Communication Compliance so you won't see them when you add a scope.

claims.claim: SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts are not supported for Communication Compliance adaptive scoping.
claims.quote: For communication compliance policies: SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts aren't supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Excluded users and Microsoft 365 groups are supported.

claims.quote: At this time, you can't use administrative units together with adaptive scopes in Communication Compliance.

claims.claim: Select adaptive scopes is hidden when a policy is scoped by administrative units.
claims.quote: If the policy is scoped by one or more admin units the Select adaptive scopes option doesn't appear.

claims.quote: Go to the Communication Compliance solution. ... Select Policies ... Select Create policy, then select Custom policy. ... On the Choose users and reviewers page: ... In the Choose users and groups section ... Select adaptive scopes

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a usable automation operation for applying adaptive scopes to Communication Compliance policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance adaptive scopes PowerShell IncludeAdaptiveScopes configure policy; "IncludeAdaptiveScopes" "Communication". Read setup guide and New-/Set-SupervisoryReviewRule references; parameter descriptions absent and setup says use portal.

claims.claim: New-SupervisoryReviewRule lists IncludeAdaptiveScopes without documenting its behaviour.
claims.quote: ### -IncludeAdaptiveScopes ... {{ Fill IncludeAdaptiveScopes Description }} ... Type: | String[]

claims.claim: The setup guide says to create and manage Communication Compliance policies in the portal rather than PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can't use PowerShell to create and manage Communication Compliance policies. You must use the Communication Compliance solution.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope opens adaptive scope creation in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... On the Adaptive scopes page, select + Create scope.
claims.fix: Keep the documented route and append to controls[1].note: 'In the wizard, keep Full directory when not restricting by administrative units, select Users or Microsoft 365 Groups, then select attributes and enter their values to build membership.' Apply the same note to the rendered row. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes#configure-adaptive-scopes.

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> -RawQuery <String> creates a scope with an advanced membership query.
claims.quote: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> -RawQuery <String> ... The RawQuery parameter switches the scope to advanced query mode. You use OPATH filter syntax for advanced query mode.

claims.claim: The New-AdaptiveScope reference describes use in retention policies, while the adaptive scopes article also covers Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: Use the New-AdaptiveScope cmdlet to create adaptive scopes in your organization. Adaptive scopes (or static scopes) are used in retention policies and retention label policies.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Risk assessment; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Membership is at Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Details > Scope details in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... Select an existing adaptive scope from the list. ... From the Details flyout pane, select Scope details.

claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity <ComplianceRuleIdParameter> -State Added retrieves current adaptive scope members.
claims.quote: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity "US Finance Users" -State Added ... This example retrieves the current members of the adaptive scope US Finance Users.

claims.claim: Query or membership changes can take up to five days to appear in scope details.
claims.quote: Moreover, adaptive scope query changes can take up to five days to become effective and reflected in the scope details view of the Adaptive Scopes page.

claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers returns at most 10,000 members on its default page.
claims.quote: For larger scopes, only the first 10,000 current members are included, and the first object in the response contains metadata with a watermark that can be used to request subsequent pages.

claims.claim: The returned Watermark is passed to PageCookie to retrieve subsequent pages.
claims.quote: To retrieve the next page, pass the Watermark value to the PageCookie parameter in your next invocation of the cmdlet.

claims.claim: The membership control is a read-only check.
claims.quote: Use this cmdlet to retrieve existing and past members (users, groups, or sites) of an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: Added in the Scope details State column identifies current members.
claims.quote: Review the State column in the list that shows Added for members within the adaptive scope or Removed if the member was previously in the adaptive scope but removed now they no longer match the scope query.

claims.claim: Role group membership is edited at Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Role groups ... Select the Communication Compliance role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group and grants its effective permissions.
claims.quote: When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group. ... The Member parameter ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins role groups can configure policies and settings.
claims.quote: | Actions | Communication Compliance | Communication Compliance Admins | ... | Configure policies and settings | Yes | Yes |

claims.claim: Role group permission changes can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After configuring your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.

claims.claim: The adaptive scope query does not run immediately.
claims.quote: Because the query doesn't run immediately, there's no validation that you typed in the value correctly.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The scope configuration does not validate that query attribute values were typed correctly.
claims.quote: Because the query doesn't run immediately, there's no validation that you typed in the value correctly.

claims.claim: Queries can take up to five days to fully populate.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for the queries to fully populate and changes aren't immediate.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises waiting a few days before attaching a new scope to a policy.
claims.quote: Factor in this delay by waiting a few days before you add a newly created scope to a policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn describes validating advanced user or group queries with Get-Recipient or Get-Mailbox in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell ... Use either Get-Recipient, Get-Mailbox, or Get-User with the -Filter parameter and your OPATH query for the adaptive scope enclosed in curly brackets

claims.claim: Policy locations are selected separately from user selection.
claims.quote: On the Choose locations to detect communications page, choose the communication channels to check, including Exchange, Teams, Viva Engage, or a specific generative AI channel.

claims.claim: Policy conditions are configured separately from user selection.
claims.quote: On the Choose conditions and review percentage page: ... In the Conditions section, add the conditions you want to detect.

claims.claim: Remediation is performed by human investigators rather than by the adaptive scope.
claims.quote: With role-based access controls, human investigators can take remediation actions such as removing a message from Teams or notifying senders of potentially inappropriate conduct.

claims.quote: When you use these commands to validate a user scope, if the number of recipients returned is higher than expected, it might be because it includes users who don't have a valid license for adaptive scopes.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate license or charge for the adaptive scoping option in Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance adaptive scopes licensing separate charge license. Read Purview service description, Adaptive scopes and Communication Compliance setup billing section; none names a separate adaptive-scoping license or meter.

claims.claim: Detecting risky interactions in non-Microsoft 365 AI data requires pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Additionally, to detect inappropriate or risky interactions for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, you need to enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: That pay-as-you-go requirement is tied to the AI data being checked, not to choosing adaptive user scopes.
claims.quote: To detect inappropriate or risky interactions for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, you need to enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: A scope is a reusable configuration element that can also be used for retention and auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: When you create a communication compliance policy, a policy for retention, or an auto-labeling policy, you can add an adaptive scope for your policy. ... As a reusable configuration element, the same adaptive scope can be used for other compliance policies.

claims.claim: Changing a shared scope's query affects the membership used by policies that select that scope.
claims.quote: As a reusable configuration element, the same adaptive scope can be used for other compliance policies. ... These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.claim: Administrative units can restrict Communication Compliance investigators to a geography or department.
claims.quote: You can use administrative units in Communication Compliance to scope user permissions to a particular geography or department. ... a German scope for investigators so that they only see user activity for German users.

claims.claim: Monitored users see nothing different when adaptive scoping is used.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance adaptive scope monitored users user experience notification changes. Read adaptive scopes, policy creation and policy settings; results describe administrator configuration but do not state that monitored users see nothing different.
claims.fix: Remove '; monitored users see nothing different' from the impact rationale. Keep the low impact judgement and its administrator-focused explanation.
